content: Nystatin and triamcinolone is a combination medication prescribed to treat fungal skin infections. It helps alleviate symptoms such as itching, inflammation, and pain. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. This medication is available in the form of an ointment or cream, which is applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used twice daily for no longer than two weeks. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before application, thoroughly clean the affected area. Apply a small amount of the cream or ointment and gently massage it into the skin until it is fully absorbed. If you are using this medication on your face, avoid contact with your eyes. If applying it to a child’s diaper area, do not use tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these can increase the absorption of triamcinolone, potentially affecting the child’s growth. Before using nystatin and triamcinolone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nystatin, triamcinolone, or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Nystatin and triamcinolone may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: acne, skin sores, itching, irritation, burning, or stinging. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Nystatin and triamcinolone is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of treatment, or if your skin condition worsens or does not improve, contact your doctor.
